A Rotary club based in Lagos has renovated an administrative block and provided eight toilets at Ajuwon Senior High School, Ogun State, in an intervention aimed at improving the school’s facilities and sanitation. The Rotary Club of Omole-Golden, District 9111, commissioned the facilities on Thursday, with the District Governor, Bukola Bakare, formally opening them for use, according to a statement made available to The PUNCH on Tuesday. The project brings the club’s community development intervention to Ajuwon, a community in Ogun State bordering Lagos, with the renovation addressing the condition of the school’s administrative building and inadequate sanitation facilities. Speaking at the commissioning, the club’s Impact President, Omowunmi Bakare, said the intervention reflected Rotary’s commitment to improving education, public health, human dignity and environmental sustainability. She said the club recognised that inadequate infrastructure could undermine the quality of education, regardless of the efforts of teachers and school administrators. However, quality education cannot thrive in an environment where essential infrastructure is inadequate,” she said. Bakare said a functional learning environment required adequate administrative facilities and hygienic sanitation infrastructure to protect students’ health and promote their general well-being. She added that the intervention aligned with Rotary’s areas of focus, particularly basic education and literacy, water, sanitation and hygiene, and environmental protection. The District Governor, Bukola Bakare, commended the club for undertaking the renovation and providing additional toilet facilities for the students. The school’s Principal, Okusaga Adejoke, said the administrative block had previously been in a deplorable condition, describing the intervention as a significant improvement to the school’s working and learning environment. She said the project went beyond physical renovation to address issues affecting the dignity, health and morale of the school community. “Rotary Club of Omole-Golden, you have done more than renovate buildings. You have restored dignity, improved health, boosted morale and created an environment where teaching and learning can truly thrive,” she said. Adejoke added that the collaboration between the club and the school demonstrated the importance of partnerships in improving educational infrastructure. A representative of the Ogun State Ministry of Education, Emmanuel Asegbe, said the state government appreciated individuals and organisations contributing to development within their communities.
